On profit: the big cloud businesses that run these data centers are very profitable. public_payload.normalized_proposition: Big tech has not profited from AI data centers and makes little generative AI revenue.

statement.excerpt: And not to repeat the point too much, but big tech has yet to actually turn anything resembling a profit on these data centers, and isn’t making much revenue at all out of generative AI.

from_speaker: has yet to actually turn anything resembling a profit
isn't making much revenue at all out of generative AI
our_interpretation: 'Big tech' is read as Microsoft, Google (Alphabet), Amazon and Meta, the four companies the surrounding text names.

'Has yet to' is cumulative. It says that from the start of the generative AI buildout (2023) through the latest results before the post (quarter ending June 2025), these companies had shown no profit from their AI data centers.
'These data centers' is read as the AI data centers whose capital spending the passage discusses, not the companies' cloud businesses as a whole.

'Isn't making much revenue at all' is read relative to the hundreds of billions in capital spending the passage discusses. In absolute terms, an informed reader might judge billions of dollars to be a lot.
criteria.support_condition: Company disclosures through the quarter ending June 2025 show no profit attributable to AI data centers, and generative AI revenue that is small next to AI capital spending.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Company disclosures through the quarter ending June 2025 show a profit attributable to AI data centers or AI services, or generative AI revenue large enough that 'not much at all' is plainly wrong.

evidence.excerpt: And our AI business has now surpassed an annual revenue run rate of $13 billion, up 175% year-over-year.
evidence.explanation: Microsoft disclosed AI revenue of more than $13 billion a year on a run-rate basis. That is a lot in absolute terms but modest next to its AI capital spending. Whether it counts as 'not much revenue at all' depends on the reading. It is also a run rate, not realised revenue.

evidence.excerpt: AWS operating income grew less than 9% to $10.2 billion as its operating expenses surged to $20.7 billion, up from $16.9 billion a year earlier.
evidence.explanation: Amazon's cloud segment, which runs its data centers including AI capacity, made $10.2 billion of operating profit in the quarter. That is a profit on data centers, but AWS does not split out the AI portion.

evidence.excerpt: higher depreciation costs from ongoing investments in AI infrastructure.
evidence.explanation: AI infrastructure costs are folded into the overall cloud segment, which stays profitable. AI-specific profit is not disclosed either way.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Company disclosure of operating profit or margin for AI infrastructure or AI services, separate from the wider cloud segment, for 2023 to mid-2025. Or an agreed threshold for what counts as 'much' generative AI revenue relative to capital spending.
